observationsNotFindings.observation: architecturesNotCrossedHere is the first explicit anti-axis guard this reviewer has seen in the input-corpus series: 'D-002 arm64/x86_64 are not a third cartesian axis of this catalog. FX-4 says both platforms.'
observationsNotFindings.whyItIsRight: Recorded as a strength. This is the only corpus so far whose source names a product AND whose surrounding decisions supply a plausible further axis — D-002's architectures are real and would have inflated the catalog from 32 to 64. Stating the refusal in the artifact, with the source of the tempting axis named, converts an absence into a checkable claim. decision.rule: ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
decision.scopeOfAccept: ACCEPT of permission-fx4-input-corpus.v1 as a DESIGN-CONTRACT-CANDIDATE at 0 blockers, 0 MUST-FIX, 0 SHOULD-FIX, with no express reservation. The artifact remains CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, binds NOTHING, and carries DO-NOT-SEAL on its own terms. It names thirty-two crash points and authors no journal bytes, no envelope and no sequence-number encoding; OBL-FX-AUTHORING is not closed and DR-105 is not SATISFIED.
decision.summaryForCoordinator: This is a permission-family subject rather than a doctor one, and it carries the largest state count reviewed in this session, so the two things I tested hardest were the product's completeness and the numeric prohibition. The product is exact: thirty-two states with thirty-two UNIQUE (transition, crashBoundary, platform) triples, so no cell is missing and none doubled, with counters of four per L-transition, sixteen per crash boundary and sixteen per platform. The recordNamed values are the interesting part, because they are assertions beyond the quoted intent — v9's FX-4 intent names no records at all — so I rebuilt the mapping from live v9's linearization.transitions and compared id by id. All eight match exactly, RA through AUD, with each transition's four states carrying one and the same record name. The sequence-number prohibition is the sharp one, because live v9 defines the counter precisely as 'a strictly increasing unsigned integer sequence number ... last durably committed sequence plus one', which is one grep away. In 23484 bytes the complete bare-integer set is 0, 1 and 26. Every encoding term returns zero — unsigned, uint, u64, width, bits, endian, 'plus one', 'starts at', monotonic. The token 'seq' occurs 36 times, which looks alarming until you resolve it: only five distinct contexts exist, all naming or negation, and 32 of the 36 are the quoted assert 'no duplicate sequence number' repeated once per state. The envelope probe is equally clean — thirteen of fifteen probed record-member names occur zero times, and the states carry eight field names between them with no nested object except the assert array. Two claims went beyond the subject's own bytes and both hold. The R-10 and R-6 attributions are exact: live G09 v3 says 'Expiry limb (R-10, named-not-authored, not a new FX identifier)' and 'the named-not-authored R-6 process-death bytes', and G09 v3 independently guards the same boundary this subject respects, recording that 'OBL-FX-AUTHORING remains the D-163 fourteen. This artifact does not widen it.' And the anti-axis guard is verified against its source: live D-002 really does read 'Platforms: macOS (arm64, x86_64) and Linux (x86_64, arm64)', so the architectures were available to cross and would have inflated this catalog from 32 to 64; the subject declines in terms and its platform pair is D-002's live set with Windows correctly absent as deferred. Custody is clean: subject unmoved at fb5783e0 and 0444 at both samplings, five of five cited digests equal live bytes, both cited standings confirmed at Claude ACCEPT 0/0 with no Codex verdict anywhere, the D-163 join confirms OBL-FX-AUTHORING still leftoverDesign true with owner none and FX-4 inside its fourteen, DR-105 OPEN and DR-G09 SPECIFIED/OPEN in live file 08, HEAD 5d5d778, required-now 26, thirty gate rows, no control bytes, and SATISFIED and QUALIFIED occur zero times. Twenty-one attacks run, twenty-one refuted, zero findings. Two things worth your attention, both favourable. The architecturesNotCrossedHere field is the first explicit anti-axis guard I have seen in this series and it is the right pattern — it converts an absence into a checkable claim and names the source of the axis it refuses. And note a trap this corpus avoided by claiming nothing: the doctor series habitually states 'the thirteen join fixtures', but the permission join names FOURTEEN FX classes; this subject says only 'the other FX classes except as named siblings', so there is no arithmetic to falsify. There is no recency claim anywhere in the artifact, so nothing here can go stale. The single nit is that the g09v3 role names R-10 and R-6 but not the G09 evidence member FX-4 actually supplies, whose live suppliedBy reads 'FX-4, FX-7. Not authored.'
